message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.21","text":"When he had said these things, I answered, “Already I give thanks to God, for just as I wished to be fully assured, so he has granted it to me. Nevertheless, be so unconcerned about matters concerning me that I will never doubt—to such a degree that, even if you yourself should ever wish to move me away from the prophetic thesis, you would be powerless and unable to do so. So well do I know what I have received. And certainly do not think that I am making you some great promise in saying this very thing, that I will never doubt. Rather, neither I myself nor any other human being who has heard the discourse concerning a prophet will ever be able to doubt the true thesis, once he has first heard and understood what the truth of prophetic proclamation is. Therefore, be confident in the teaching willed by God, for every craft of evil has been defeated. Against prophecy nothing has any power: neither verbal arts nor contrivances of sophisms, neither syllogisms nor any other device—provided, at least, that the one who has listened to a true prophet genuinely desires truth and is not, under the pretext of truth, looking around for something else. So, my lord Peter, do not lose heart as though you had bestowed the greatest good on someone without perception. For you bestowed it on one who perceives the favor and cannot be led astray from the truth that was given. For I know that there are things a person wants both to receive quickly and not to obtain slowly. Therefore I know not to despise, because of its speed, the incomparable and only secure thing given to me.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὡς γὰρ ἐβουλόμην πληροφορηθῆναι","chosen":"just as I wished to be fully assured","rationale":"The passive πληροφορηθῆναι denotes attaining full assurance rather than merely receiving information."},{"source_quote":"τῆς προφητικῆς ὑποθέσεως","chosen":"the prophetic thesis","rationale":"Ὑπόθεσις denotes the position or foundational proposition concerning prophecy; “thesis” preserves that conceptual sense."},{"source_quote":"προφητικῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἀλήθεια","chosen":"the truth of prophetic proclamation","rationale":"In context, ἐπαγγελία can denote a declaration or profession; “promise” remains a possible lexical alternative."},{"source_quote":"τῷ θεοβουλήτῳ δόγματι","chosen":"the teaching willed by God","rationale":"This renders the compound θεοβούλητος explicitly while taking δόγμα as an authoritative teaching."},{"source_quote":"οὔτε τέχναι λόγων οὔτε σοφισμάτων ἐπίνοιαι, οὐ συλλογισμοί, οὐκ ἄλλη τις μηχανή","chosen":"neither verbal arts nor contrivances of sophisms, neither syllogisms nor any other device","rationale":"The rendering preserves the ordered list of rhetorical arts, devised sophisms, formal arguments, and other mechanisms."},{"source_quote":"οὐ προφάσει ἀληθείας ἕτερόν τι περιβλέπεται","chosen":"is not, under the pretext of truth, looking around for something else","rationale":"Περιβλέπεται retains the image of looking about for another objective while using truth as a pretext."},{"source_quote":"μὴ ἀθύμει ὡς ἀναισθήτῳ τὸ μέγιστον δωρησάμενος ἀγαθόν· αἰσθομένῳ γὰρ χάριτος ἐδωρήσω","chosen":"do not lose heart as though you had bestowed the greatest good on someone without perception. For you bestowed it on one who perceives the favor","rationale":"“Without perception” and “perceives” preserve the contrast between ἀναίσθητος and αἰσθάνομαι."},{"source_quote":"ἀπατηθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δοθέντος ἀληθοῦς","chosen":"be led astray from the truth that was given","rationale":"The neuter substantive ἀληθές is rendered “truth,” while ἀπό is given separative force."},{"source_quote":"ἔνεστιν ὧν βούλεταί τις καὶ ταχέως λαβεῖν καὶ βραδέως μὴ τυχεῖν","chosen":"there are things a person wants both to receive quickly and not to obtain slowly","rationale":"Βούλεται governs both coordinated infinitival expressions, preserving the contrast between quick and delayed acquisition."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ δοθέντος μοι διὰ τὸ τάχος ἀσυγκρίτου καὶ μόνου ἀσφαλοῦς","chosen":"because of its speed, the incomparable and only secure thing given to me","rationale":"The genitive adjectives describe what was given, while διὰ τὸ τάχος states the possible ground for undervaluing it."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.22","text":"After I had said these things, Peter said, “I acknowledge my gratitude to God both for your salvation and for my own enjoyment. For I truly rejoice, knowing that you have recognized just what the greatness of prophecy is. Since, then, as you said, even if I myself should ever wish—may that never happen!—to move you over to another teaching, I would be unable to persuade you, begin from tomorrow onward to be present with me at the debates with the opponents. Tomorrow I am to face Simon the magician.” After saying this and himself partaking of food, he instructed me too to partake separately. Then, after offering a blessing over the food and giving thanks, after being satisfied and having also given me the explanation of this very matter, he went on to say, “May God grant you to become like me in every respect and, once you have been baptized, to share the same table with me.” After saying this, he instructed me to rest, for by then, I suppose, the nature of the body was demanding sleep as well.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Χάριν ὁμολογῶ τῷ θεῷ","chosen":"I acknowledge my gratitude to God","rationale":"Ὁμολογῶ gives the thanksgiving the force of an expressed acknowledgment."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τῆς ἐμῆς ἀπολαύσεως","chosen":"for my own enjoyment","rationale":"Ἀπόλαυσις denotes Peter’s own enjoyment or delight arising from Clement’s response."},{"source_quote":"ὅπερ ἀπείη","chosen":"may that never happen!","rationale":"The optative expresses a strong wish that the contemplated change of teaching remain far removed."},{"source_quote":"ἄρξαι τοῦ λοιποῦ ἀπὸ τῆς αὔριον παρεῖναί μοι","chosen":"begin from tomorrow onward to be present with me","rationale":"“From tomorrow onward” represents both ἀπὸ τῆς αὔριον and the prospective force of τοῦ λοιποῦ."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ταῖς τῶν ἀντικειμένων ζητήσεσιν","chosen":"at the debates with the opponents","rationale":"Ζητήσεις denotes adversarial discussions here, and the genitive identifies the opposing participants."},{"source_quote":"ἔστι δέ μοι ἡ αὔριον πρὸς Σίμωνα μάγον","chosen":"Tomorrow I am to face Simon the magician","rationale":"The idiomatic English preserves the prospective sense and the adversarial force of πρός; μάγον is treated as a descriptive designation."},{"source_quote":"ἰδία κἀμὲ μεταλαβεῖν ἐκέλευσεν","chosen":"he instructed me too to partake separately","rationale":"The rendering follows the apparent intended adverbial sense and associates it with Clement’s partaking; the later contrast with sharing Peter’s table supports separation, though the printed form is problematic."},{"source_quote":"αὐτοῦ τούτου τὸν λόγον μοι ἀποδοὺς","chosen":"having also given me the explanation of this very matter","rationale":"Τὸν λόγον ἀποδιδόναι here most naturally means supplying the reason or explanation for the matter just described."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ πάντα ἐξομοιωθῆναί μοι","chosen":"to become like me in every respect","rationale":"The passive ἐξομοιωθῆναι expresses being brought into likeness, with κατὰ πάντα specifying every respect."},{"source_quote":"βαπτισθέντα τῆς αὐτῆς μοι μεταλαβεῖν τραπέζης","chosen":"once you have been baptized, to share the same table with me","rationale":"The participle presents baptism as antecedent to participation, and μεταλαβεῖν with the genitive is rendered “share.”"},{"source_quote":"ἤδη γάρ που καὶ τὸν ὕπνον ἀπῄτει ἡ τοῦ σώματος φύσις","chosen":"for by then, I suppose, the nature of the body was demanding sleep as well","rationale":"The enclitic που gives the statement a mildly tentative or inferential force."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἰδία","issue":"The printed form is difficult in the apparent adverbial syntax. The expected standard adverbial form would have a different accent and an iota subscript. The placement also leaves some uncertainty about whether “separately” modifies Peter’s partaking or Clement’s.","proposed_reading":"ἰδίᾳ","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
